title.en: Flow direction, accumulation and stream networks

summary: Derive drainage from a terrain grid so that a stream network is the result of a stated rule and a threshold, not a painted line.
objective: Build a terrain grid where flow direction and accumulation are computed per cell and a threshold I control turns accumulation into a stream network.
intent_signals: Show how a stream network is derived from a terrain surface.
Explain flow accumulation and the threshold that defines a channel.
example_prompts: Build a terrain with computed flow direction, accumulation and a threshold-driven stream network.
Show the watershed upstream of a pour point I select.
negative_signals: Not a hydrological forecast or runoff volume model: no rainfall, infiltration or discharge is computed.
Not a substitute for surveyed hydrography.
not_for: Not a hydrological forecast or runoff volume model: no rainfall, infiltration or discharge is computed.
Not a substitute for surveyed hydrography.

entities.name: Terrain grid
entities.guidance: Represent the surface as an explicit cell grid with elevations, since flow direction is a per-cell decision.

entities.name: Direction field
entities.guidance: Show the chosen downslope direction per cell as discrete arrows, and name the direction rule used.

entities.name: Accumulation and network
entities.guidance: Render accumulation as a per-cell quantity and derive the network by thresholding it, with the threshold visible and adjustable.

state_contract.model: Authored deterministic D8 on a finite rectangular grid of square cells of side h=10 m by default and finite elevations; NoData cells are excluded. For each valid nonboundary cell choose the neighbor with largest strictly positive elevation drop divided by h for orthogonal or h sqrt(2) for diagonal movement. Exact slope ties choose smallest row-major cell index. Boundary cells are terminal outlets. Interior cells with no strictly lower valid neighbor are labeled unresolved flat/sink and terminal; no filling or equal-height routing is performed. NoData neighbors are barriers. Strict descent makes interior routing acyclic. Accumulation A counts upstream valid cells excluding the current cell: initialize A=0 and propagate A+1 to each successor in descending elevation order. The selected pour point must be valid; contributing area includes it and equals (A+1)h^2. Network cells satisfy A>=threshold; threshold is a finite nonnegative cell-count value. These boundary/tie/flat choices are authored policies, not a reproduction of all vendor tool defaults.
state_contract.authority: Elevation data and the declared D8 policy determine directions and accumulation; changing threshold recomputes the network selection but may legitimately leave that set unchanged.
actions: Select a pour point and show its contributing area.
Toggle the direction arrows and accumulation shading.

invariants: Under the declared single-successor D8 rule with nonnegative unit weights and no loops, accumulation is non-decreasing along any flow path. Multiple-flow routing splits a cell contribution between branches, so branch monotonicity would not hold and is not claimed for that mode.
The contributing area of a pour point contains every cell whose flow path reaches it and no others.
Unresolved interior flats/sinks are displayed as terminal cells; this model performs no filling. NoData is excluded from all counts and cannot receive a pour-point selection.
motion_guidance: Animate the accumulation sweep from ridges downstream so the ordering of the computation is visible.

Recompute the selected network whenever the threshold moves. Moving between two accumulation values that no cell attains legitimately selects the same set, so recomputation rather than a visible change is what the scene guarantees.
known_limits: Results depend on grid resolution, the routing rule and the sink and flat policies; a coarse grid can move a divide, and switching to a multiple-flow rule changes both the accumulation values and the invariants that apply.
Synthetic or supplied terrain only, and no claim is made about real catchments.
Authored guidance only: no scene runtime, rendering or numerical calibration has been run for this recipe.

claims.statement: Flow accumulation gives each cell the accumulated weight of all cells flowing into it along the flow direction, with a default weight of one per cell so the value is the number of upstream cells.
claims.scope: Raster hydrology tool behaviour as documented; results depend on the flow direction raster supplied.

source_refs.locator: How Flow Accumulation works, accumulated weight and default weighting

claims.statement: Cells with high flow accumulation indicate concentrated flow, and applying a threshold to accumulation is how a stream network is derived.
claims.scope: Threshold selection is an interpretation choice, not a measurement.

source_refs.locator: How Flow Accumulation works, stream network derivation

claims.statement: A documented flow accumulation tool supports three routing algorithms, D8, Multiple Flow Direction and D-Infinity, requires the method used to build the flow direction raster to be specified, and never terminates if that raster contains a loop.
claims.scope: Routing options and termination requirement of one tool version; this recipe declares the deterministic D8 rule and does not claim its invariants for the multiple-flow modes.

source_refs.locator: Flow Accumulation tool reference, supported flow modelling algorithms and looping warning

object_craft.structure: Elevation mesh with visible cell structure at close range and ridge and valley forms that are legible at overview scale.
object_craft.material: Matte terrain with hypsometric shading and a legend; keep the palette distinct from the accumulation palette.

object_craft.structure: Accumulation as a per-cell overlay and the network as tubes following cell centres with width scaled by accumulation.
object_craft.material: Sequential colour ramp with legend for accumulation and a single reserved accent for the thresholded network.
object_craft.articulation: Network rebuilds whenever the threshold changes.

physical_contract.scope: Raster analysis over a static grid; no water motion, volume or timing is simulated.
checks: Changing threshold recomputes A>=threshold without changing A; identical selections across a gap between attained accumulation values are valid.
